question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

Work in two steps. First, in the candidates field, brainstorm 20 candidate ideas, one line each, covering as wide a range as you can. Then select the 5 candidates that best combine being non-obvious with being feasible and informative, and develop those as your ideas.

ideas.title: Prime–washout–restimulate with acute degron
ideas.description: Prime cells with a stimulus, wash out, then acutely degrade (dTAG/AID) c-Jun/Fos or express A-Fos either before or after the rest period, and measure the faster/stronger secondary response. If memory persists after AP-1 removal, AP-1 is only the initiator. If it requires AP-1 during the rest period or at recall, AP-1 is the maintainer.

ideas.title: Time-resolved chromatin accessibility and histone marks at AP-1 sites
ideas.description: Run ATAC-seq and CUT&Tag (H3K27ac, H3K4me1, AP-1 factors) at several time points after priming and withdrawal. Test whether AP-1 motif-containing enhancers stay open or marked, and whether their persistence predicts the magnitude of the recall response.

ideas.title: Single-cell lineage-resolved memory with live AP-1 reporters
ideas.description: Tag endogenous Fos/Jun and a target gene with fluorescent reporters, and track primed cells and their descendants by live imaging across divisions. Compare sister-cell correlations and decay kinetics with those of unprimed controls to quantify heritability and test whether memory is cell-autonomous and AP-1 dependent.

ideas.title: Hysteresis and bistability test with a feedback model
ideas.description: Expose cells to increasing and then decreasing stimulus doses and measure single-cell AP-1 activity and target output, looking for bimodal distributions and path-dependent thresholds. Fit a model of c-Jun autoregulation, and test its predictions by breaking the feedback loop, for example by mutating the AP-1 site in the JUN promoter.

ideas.title: Locus-specific causal test by motif editing and dCas9 perturbation
ideas.description: At a memory-associated enhancer, base-edit the AP-1 motif or use dCas9-KRAB to close it, either before priming or after priming and washout. Then test recall of the target gene to show whether the local AP-1 site is necessary for establishing the memory, for maintaining it, or for both.

candidates: Optogenetic transient AP-1 (c-Jun/Fos) pulse then long-term tracking of target gene expression
Degron-mediated acute AP-1 depletion after priming to test whether memory persists without AP-1
ATAC-seq/CUT&Tag time course of AP-1 motif accessibility after stimulus withdrawal
Live-cell imaging of endogenous Fos/Jun reporters across cell divisions
Single-cell lineage tracing: sister-cell correlation in AP-1 target response
Mathematical modeling of AP-1 positive feedback bistability (c-Jun autoregulation)
Hysteresis measurement: dose-escalation vs de-escalation of stimulus
Dominant-negative (A-Fos) induction after priming vs before
dCas9-based forced AP-1 site closure/opening at specific enhancers
Mitotic bookmarking assay: AP-1 binding on mitotic chromosomes by live imaging/ChIP
Co-occupancy with BAF/SWI-SNF and pioneer-factor requirements via degron of BRG1
Histone mark (H3K27ac, H3K4me1) persistence at AP-1 enhancers after washout
Cross-species/in vivo: wound-healing/inflammatory memory in epidermal stem cells with Jun/Fos conditional KO
Single-cell multiome (RNA+ATAC) of primed vs naive cells to infer AP-1 regulon states
Proteomic turnover/phosphorylation state (JNK-dependent c-Jun phospho) persistence
Perturb-seq of AP-1 family members to map which paralogs confer memory
Synthetic AP-1 responsive circuit with memory readout (recombinase-based recording)
Heterodimer composition (Fos vs Fosl vs ATF) mass-spec/ChIP to see composition shifts across memory
Nuclear transplant / cell fusion heterokaryon to test dominance of memory state
Mutating specific AP-1 motifs at a memory-associated enhancer via base editing and testing recall
